body:
`uv workspace metadata` omits installed distributions that are absent from the lockfile, including their module ownership. This prevents consumers such as ty from identifying imports supplied by packages left over in the environment.

For example, with uv 0.12.6:

1. Install two independent project dependencies.
2. Remove one with `uv remove --no-sync`, updating the declarations and lockfile while preserving the environment.
3. Run ty through `uv run`, with `missing-direct-dependency` enabled.

The removed package remains importable, but it is absent from both `resolution` and `module_owners`. ty therefore reports neither an unresolved import nor a missing direct dependency. Running `uv sync` removes the package and makes the unresolved import visible.

uv already has a [test covering the ownership omission](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/blob/7938ca5d53dbb9c614a4a030df406e41ff101ab9/crates/uv/tests/workspace/workspace_metadata.rs#L882-L924), and the filtering remains in 0.12.8. Reporting every import with unknown ownership would produce false positives, since ownership information can also be incomplete for valid imports.

Workspace metadata should expose these installed distributions and the modules they provide, while keeping installed state distinct from the locked dependency graph. This would let ty identify imports from extraneous packages without modifying the environment or duplicating uv’s installed-package inspection.

Related: #10962 and the [installed-package metadata discussion on #19122](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/19122#discussion_r3154901317).
title: Expose module ownership for installed packages outside the lockfile
